cards.text: Abram just chased down four kings with 318 trained men born in his household and rescued his nephew Lot (Genesis 14:14-16). Then he turned down even a sandal strap from the king of Sodom (Genesis 14:22-23). After these events, the word of the LORD comes to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward."
Abram answers God with a question: "O Lord GOD, what can You give me…"

cards.question: Abram asks God what He can give him. What does Abram say he still doesn't have?

cards.text: So with no children, who gets everything when Abram is gone? Abram says the heir of his house is Eliezer of Damascus.

cards.question: Abram says God has given him no offspring, so a ___ in his household will be his heir.
When the word of the LORD comes to Abram again, God says Eliezer of Damascus will be his heir after all.

cards.text: God says Abram's heir will be one who comes from his own body. Then the LORD takes Abram outside and tells him to look to the heavens.

cards.question: God tells Abram to count the ___ if he is able. Then God says his ___ will be like that.
Abram has no children, and God just promised him offspring like the stars. What does Abram do?

cards.text: "Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness." Abram gets a sky FULL of stars to count, and I got years of counting dust in a junk drawer: same hobby, VERY different view!
Then the LORD tells Abram, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans…" God's reminding Abram where this whole journey started.

cards.question: God says He brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give him this ___ to possess.

cards.text: Abram has a question about that land, and friend, I can't judge. When the angel showed up at my junk drawer, one of my first questions was whether he had the right drawer.

cards.question: What does Abram ask the Lord GOD about the land?

answers.text: How he can know he will possess it
How far its borders will reach
When his family should move there

cards.text: The LORD answers, "Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon." Abram asks ONE question and gets back a whole LIST, ages included!

cards.question: Abram brings God every animal and bird on that list.

cards.text: Abram splits each animal down the middle and lays the halves opposite each other, but he doesn't cut the birds in half. Then birds of prey come down on the carcasses.

cards.question: Abram lets the birds of prey have the carcasses.

cards.text: Now it gets heavy. "As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him."
Then the LORD says to Abram, "Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years."

cards.question: God says He will judge the nation that Abram's descendants serve as slaves.
Abram's descendants are strangers in a land that isn't theirs. After God judges the nation that enslaves them, what happens to them?

answers.text: They stay and rule over that nation
They scatter among the other nations

cards.question: God tells Abram he will live to see his descendants come back to this land.

cards.text: God says Abram himself will go to his fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.

cards.question: God says Abram's descendants will return here in the fourth generation. The reason it's not sooner has to do with the Amorites, one of the peoples of this land. What is it?

answers.text: Their sin is not yet complete
Their cities are not yet built
Their army is not yet weak

cards.text: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appear. Friend, this is the part of the story where I lean in close.

cards.question: The smoking firepot and the flaming torch pass between the halves of the carcasses Abram laid out.
Abram asked how he could know the land would be his. On the day the firepot and torch pass through, what does the LORD do?

cards.text: God says He has given this land to Abram's descendants, from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates. Friend, my whole planet is just big enough for ONE bakery!

Then God names the ten peoples whose land it is, from the Kenites to the Jebusites, and yes, the Amorites are on the list. That's where we leave Abram for now, friend, but this story is FAR from done.
